title: Offering food, best dharma
content_html:
Offering food to others is the best dharma, said R. Narayanan in a discourse. There is nothing to equal this, says Tiruvalluvar. In his Tirumanthiram, Tirumoolar says we should offer a vilva leaf to Lord Siva, grass to a cow, and food to fellow human beings. More importantly, we must always use sweet words. Tiruvalluvar says that even nectar, which confers immortality, must be shared with others.

Ilayankudi Maranar was one of the 63 Nayanmars praised by Sekkizhar in his Periya Puranam. Maranar was wealthy. He honoured devotees of Siva by washing their feet with scented water. He then offered them a lavish meal, which did not lack any flavour. The Lord wanted to show the world how generous Ilayankudi Maranar could be even in poverty. He made sure that Maranar lost his wealth. Eventually, he was left with nothing but a tiled house and a small plot of land. One night, after Maranar had sown seeds in his field, it rained heavily. That night, Siva, in the guise of a Saivite devotee, arrived at Maranar’s doorstep. Maranar’s wife asked her husband to fetch the grains that had been sown that morning. She cleaned the grains, and used it to cook rice for the visitor. Usually, the grains used for sowing were never used for cooking, because they ensured that a farmer would be able to grow his next crop. So, something that would take care of a farmer’s future would never be used for food. But Maranar and his wife broke that rule, when they cooked for the mendicant. Greens grown in the backyard were also used to prepare tasty dishes. Since there was no firewood, Maranar’s wife used a wooden beam from their house as firewood. When the couple was about to serve food, the sleeping guest woke and revealed Himself as Lord Siva. He blessed them and said they would reach Sivaloka.

title: Ujjal Biswas, former Bengal minister dies after prolonged illness, Mamata expresses grief
author: PTI
content_html:
Former West Bengal minister and senior TMC leader Ujjal Biswas died at a private hospital in Kolkata on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) after battling multiple health complications for nearly three weeks, hospital sources said.

He was 72 and is survived by wife and son.

Mr. Biswas, who was admitted to Fortis Hospital in Mukundapur, had been on full ventilator support for the past few days.

The former minister had developed multiple complications following a bypass surgery, after which he suffered a brain stroke. His condition subsequently deteriorated, with pneumonia, urinary tract infection and septic shock further aggravating his health problems. He also suffered severe kidney dysfunction and had been undergoing dialysis.

The complications had raised concerns over multiple organ failure, according to medical updates.

"Just came to know that Ujjal Biswas passed away this evening around 9 pm. I am on my way to the hospital," TMC MLA Kunal Ghosh said.

Mr. Biswas, who had served as the State's correctional administration minister during the TMC regime, was arrested on June 10 in connection with alleged misappropriation of government relief materials in Nadia district's Krishnanagar.

His arrest came hours after an angry crowd allegedly stormed his residence, threw eggs and raised slogans against him over the alleged recovery of government relief supplies, including tarpaulins, dhotis, sarees and clothes, from his house.

Protesters had gheraoed the former minister at his residence for nearly an hour, following which police detained him and took him to Kotwali Police Station, where his arrest was formally recorded.

He was subsequently released on bail in July.

Former chief minister Mamata Banerjee expressed grief over the death of Biswas, alleging that he was subjected to "political persecution, physical assault and mental harassment in the final months of his life."

In a condolence message on X, Banerjee described Biswas as "much more than a colleague in public life", saying they shared a close bond built over several years.

Ms. Banerjee said Mr. Biswas had devoted his life to the Trinamool Congress and the service of the people, describing his loyalty and commitment as invaluable to the party.

Ms. Banerjee also referred to "the difficult period" Mr. Biswas allegedly went through following the change in the political situation in the State, claiming that he was "brutally attacked, implicated in false cases and kept behind bars for 49 days."

Recalling a meeting with the former minister, she said he had personally narrated the alleged torture, humiliation and intimidation he faced for refusing to abandon his political convictions or switch sides.

His ordeal, Ms. Banerjee alleged, reflected the BJP's "politics of vengeance, intimidation and persecution in West Bengal."

"No political rivalry can justify such cruelty. No government has the right to turn the machinery of the state into an instrument of political retribution," she said.

Describing his death as a personal loss, Banerjee said she had lost someone with whom she shared "years of trust, affection and solidarity."

Ms. Banerjee extended her condolences to the bereaved family, saying Mr. Biswas's courage, loyalty and lifelong commitment to public service would remain etched in the memories of those who knew him.

title: Suvendu-Abhishek feud keeps political temperatures high in West Bengal
author: Shiv Sahay Singh
content_html:
Six months after the West Bengal Assembly election, the feud between Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari and All India Trinamool Congress (AITC) leader Abhishek Banerjee continues to dominate the State’s politics.

The Assembly election defeat and the subsequent split in the Trinamool Congress (TMC), with a majority of its Lok Sabha MPs and MLAs breaking away from Mamata Banerjee, have posed an existential threat to the former Chief Minister and her nephew. Mr. Abhishek, particularly, has come under fire from both the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and critics of Ms. Mamata. While the BJP has accused him of corruption during the TMC’s rule, party rebels have held him responsible for the electoral setback and cited his leadership as a reason for quitting the party.

title: Owaisi, Azad likely to announce alliance on November 12 for Uttar Pradesh elections
author: Mayank Kumar
content_html:
All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) president Asaduddin Owaisi and Azad Samaj Party (Kanshiram) chief Chandrashekhar Azad are likely to announce a political alliance for the 2027 State Assembly elections at a joint press conference in Lucknow on Thursday, November 12.

The likely alliance between the two parties could pave the way for a first declared non-Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), non-Congress political front in Uttar Pradesh, with both parties considered marginal players eyeing to consolidate Scheduled Caste (SC) and minority voters in the politically crucial state.

Both the Nagina MP, Chandrashekhar Azad and Hyderabad MP Owaisi separately arrived in Lucknow though they did not reveal the details of their alliance or the joint presser expected in the State capital on Thursday (November 12, 2026).

 

“The alliance will be aiming to focus on Dalit and minority voters, as both leaders since long are associated with these vote blocks, but getting votes or winning your own seat and making your candidates victorious is a different issue,” said Asad Rizvi, a political analyst based in Lucknow, adding that the State is increasingly transforming into bipolar politics, between NDA and INDIA bloc, and it would be a huge challenge for the new alliance to make an impact.

title: Why are fertility centres in Hyderabad in crosshairs over human egg harvesting? Explained
author: Serish Nanisetti
content_html:
The story so far: Hyderabad has emerged as healthcare hub in India with a large number of private hospitals providing state of the art healthcare. Simultaneously, there has been a surge in number of fertility centres that promise successful childbirth for couples finding it difficult to have children. There are advertisements on autorickshaws and even bus bays promising a range of fertility treatments for couples finding it difficult to have children. In the last week of October, the Telangana police raided three premises and rescued 29 women from six states who were kept in confinement for harvesting their oocytes (eggs).

IUI or Intrauterine Insemination, IVF or in-vitro fertilisation, ICSI (Intracytoplasmic Sperm Injection), are some of the fertility procedures that these centres provide at a cost to help parents conceive. Along with these medical procedures, these specialised centres were performing other related interventions like ovarian stimulation, egg retrieval, embryo transfer, surgical sperm retrieval and frozen embryo transfer. And all the processes are part of the packages that range from ₹2.5 lakh to ₹50 lakh depending on the Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) services.
